_comment: Why each class of ident_fix collision is harmless (F0-D, 27B). Pairs are (old German word -> English target); the target already exists in the file.

python_no_scope_meets.why: hazard check (AST): in no scope both words are bound/used as binding; no call passes both as keywords; no dict literal and no access on the same base carries both as key. Typical: the old word is a dict key / keyword of one record, the target is a local, a parameter, an attribute (`.values()`) or a key of another record. propose.py: the duplicate lies in one startswith() tuple (`("geborgt", "unbelegt", "borrowed", ...)`): a tuple with the same prefix twice is harmless.

python_disambiguated_in_source.why: both words DID meet (parameter `state` of _entry next to `zustand`, two `state=` keywords in one call after renaming; local `notes` next to local `hinweise`). Source disambiguated before the run (commit F0-D pre-rename): _entry(state=...) -> verdict_state, local hinweise -> hint_list. Keys of the records (`"zustand"` entry key, `"state"` inside the nested `verdikt` dict; `fit["hinweise"]`) stay and are renamed by the table.

shell_and_markdown.why: the target word occurs only in comments/prose/paths (`/sys/class/...`, `evidence` in a header comment); no shell variable or function of the target name. Side effect named, not a collision: launch_when_free.sh line 31 `session=agent-332-fam-beleg` (a historic holder session id compared with the holder file) becomes `...fam-evidence` -- the whole-word rule of ident_fix; the script is a one-off of ticket 332.

catalog_json.why: key/value walk: the English target is a value or a key of ANOTHER object than the old word (`anzeige.rel.braucht: "requires"` is a display map whose key is renamed to the same word as its value; `datei` is a key of the `beleg` records, `file` of the `source` records; root `trees` vs `entries.*.baeume`). The file is rebuilt in F0-F anyway.

web_js_html.why: IDENT_FIX_WEB=1: the dashboard pages read the keys the planner modules write; line reading of every old-word line plus a regex check for the target as declared identifier/key in the same file. Targets (`value`, `source`, `title`, `note`, `state`) occur as DOM properties (`el.value`), other data objects (`f.value` in the IPC table, `c.title`), or prose. No object literal and no function carries both words as properties/variables of the same object.
